title: Donor-held-out tests gave higher delay error in two selected Allen inhibitory slice samples with fixed linear models
abstract: We tested how the validation unit changes synaptic delay prediction error in Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 small. We used 2,534 detected connections in mouse visual cortex and human temporal cortex, at cell-body distances up to 500 micrometres. Fixed class, layer and distance ridge models used the same training count in edge, recording and inferred-donor splits. Across 20 repeated five-fold tests, human inhibitory RMSE rose from 1.180 ms in edge splits to 1.684 ms in donor splits. Mouse inhibitory RMSE rose from 0.469 to 0.473 ms. Donor-minus-edge mean squared error gaps were 1.443 and 0.00345 ms squared. Conditional 98.75 percent donor bootstrap intervals were above zero in both samples. The two excitatory samples had intervals that included zero. A stronger ridge penalty retained the inhibitory result. Removal of any single donor from the fixed test errors kept both inhibitory gaps positive. The human result had only 61 connections from 25 inferred donors and was strongly affected by a large donor. These tests show a validation dependence for the tested models. They do not identify its biological cause or prove a general rule. New code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external regeneration steps are supplied.

display.caption: Delay prediction error under three validation units, with equal training counts. Intervals condition on the fitted models. Ex means excitatory. In means inhibitory.
